messages:
Nina: quick follow-up from the RFC — proposing a lightweight "soft-launch fanout" pattern that lets us ramp traffic to a new variant while keeping an automatic, deterministic rollback path.

Raj: sketch it out, pls. is this central decisioning or local? :thinking_face:

Nina: idea: central coordinator decides initial fanout percentages, observers (local) run probes and emit signal summaries back. coordinator reduces fanout when net-signal < threshold. fallback is pre-wired and deterministic.

Leah: so observer = per-pod probe runner? what signals are we aggregating?

Nina: yes, per-host observer. signals: latency p95, error-rate, quality-regression score (from eval hooks), and a lightweight drift metric. each signal -> 3-state: OK / WARN / FAIL. aggregator tallies weighted votes.

Tom: weights configurable per route. good. what about reaction latency? we don't want flapping for transient spikes.

Nina: introduce a short "hysteresis window" plus a decaying evidence buffer. aggregator exposes a single scalar called `safety_delta` in [-1.0,1.0]. negative -> more likely to shrink traffic. values smoothed over configurable half-life.

Sasha: how is rollback executed? immediate cut or gradual?

Nina: deterministic policy: if safety_delta <= -0.7 for 3 consecutive windows -> immediate circuit to baseline. else if between -0.3 and -0.7 -> step down fanout by configured step % per window. allows both hard and soft exits.

Raj: boundary question — should the coordinator actually abort in-band (drop traffic) or reply with route hints and let proxy enforce?

Leah: prefer proxy-enforced hints. keep coordinator AS a planner/observer so control plane outage can't kill traffic. proxies already have rate/route logic.

Tom: agree. coordinator emits `RouteAction { variant, desired_share, cutoff_flag }`. proxies reconcile with local quotas.

Nina: also propose a simple rollback DSL stored in the deployment: `on: [signal_specs] action: [stepdown | immediate | hold] meta: [notify]`. example:

```
on: [- latency_p95 > 1200ms, error_rate > 0.05]
action: immediate
meta: notify=#oncall, annotate=rollback-cause
```

Sasha: love the DSL. where do we run probe evals for "quality-regression score"? shadow traffic sampler?

Nina: have a small sampled mirror (1%) routed to a scorer service. scorer returns token-level heuristics and an aggregated score. scoring runs asynchronously and contributes to safety_delta with a longer half-life.

Raj: telemetry volume concerns. if every pod sends full traces that explodes.

Leah: don't ship full traces — observers emit compressed histograms and small counters (json summary). we keep sample ids for audit only. retention short (24h) for aggregator windows.

Tom: what about operator override / breakglass?

Nina: two-tier override: `soft_override` (bias planner but still respects strong fail signals) and `hard_override` (immediate freeze state, needs manual clear). ops-bot will post override and sls entry.

deploy-bot: Deployment 2024-12-08T15:07 started: variant=v2, initial_fanout=5% :rocket:

Sasha: nice. question on testing: we should have a deterministic sim harness that feeds synthetic signals and asserts final traffic curve.

Raj: yep — add a unit-test harness that runs coordinator state machine with replayed windows. also run chaos tests where observer drops are simulated.

Leah: integration note: proxies need a `safe_cutoff` API to receive cutoff_flag. minimal surface: `PATCH /route/:id/desired_share {percent, cutoff}`. simple and robust.

Tom: ops SLO interaction — if the coordinator is unavailable, proxies should continue with last known share and apply local backoff if latency > local_threshold.

Nina: tradeoffs we called out:
- central planner = simpler global view, more control, single point of failure
- proxy-driven enforcement = resilient, local autonomy but complicates global quotas
- strong immediate rollback improves safety but risks overreacting to noisy signals

Nina: next steps: 1) add coordinator proto + aggregator summary schema 2) prototype DSL parser + unit harness 3) proxy API change (PATCH) 4) pilot on non-critical route.

Sasha: 👍 Will take DSL parser.

Raj: I'll do aggregator schema and sim harness.

Leah: i'll PR proxy API and add docs for signal payload.

Tom: I'll own rollout playbook + SLO tuning guidance.

Nina: thanks team — I'll open an RFC follow-up with links to sketches and the sim harness ticket. tagging @oncall for visibility. :eyes:

deploy-bot: Note: 5% fanout to v2 active; observers live.
